title: Selective Memory Deletion in a Hyperpersonalized AI OS — Distributed Storage and Provenance-Based Recomputation
content: Deleting a personal memory from an AI assistant changes what the system may use for personalization. The effects of that memory can survive in summaries, recommendation rules, or inputs assembled on another device. We evaluate whether AURAI, a data OS for hyperpersonalized AI, can withdraw one confirmed memory and its influence while preserving records supported by independent evidence. In an isolated prototype using AURAI code, a deletion propagated between two emulated devices. The receiving device rebuilt its daily view without the deleted preference, preserved an independent routine completion and its source, and excluded the preference from both assembled dialogue contexts. In a separate local case, a recommendation remained active while its recorded support fell from two sources to one. Eleven functional cases met their expected states. One additional case reproduced stale memory text in the input during a server read failure. A separate live integration case verified that two model APIs received post-deletion inputs without the target text and with an independent memory intact. In a 30-condition simulation, a missing reverse dependency edge could leave the displayed recommendation correct while its provenance still named the deleted source. These results establish feasibility for the evaluated local paths and motivate separate checks of displayed values and their supporting evidence.
